transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jia Chen (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz (Horizon InfoSec), Tom Becker (Horizon Cloud), Priya Singh (Procurement), Evan Lee (Legal)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this to about 45-60 minutes, we wanted to run through the SIG / vendor risk questionnaire, call out where we can attach evidences and capture follow ups, i'm Samir, i'm the AE, with me is jia our security tec eng, and luis from customer success.
[00:20] Marta (Horizon): thanks, yep im marta, i'm the info sec lead, we've got tom on infra and priya on procurement, evan for legal. main items for us are SOC 2, data residency for EU and US east, SSO, audit logs and how redwood handles keys.
[00:34] Jia (Redwood): great, quick agenda, i'll do a run through of the SIG sections, call out standard evidence we attach (SOC2 report, iso certs, pen test summary, network diagram, logging playbooks), and then we'll note anything that needs a custom artifact like BYOK diagrams. quick note: when i say Redwood Private or Redwood Dedicated, sometimes the automated notes spell it differently in the questionnaire.
[01:05] Tom (Horizon): one ask up front: do you support BYOK and HSM integration for customer-managed keys? and can we rotate without downtime?
[01:20] Jia (Redwood): yes we support BYOK via our KMS integrations — we have a KMS adapter pattern, you can bring keys from AWS KMS, Google KMS, or use an HSM-backed provider via standard KMIP or customer managed HSM. key rotation is supported and is rolling with no end-user outage, we do key versioning and rewrap tokens. i'll send the KMS architecture diagram after the call.
[01:45] Marta (Horizon): what's the control around key access? are keys ever in plaintext on your side?
[01:50] Jia (Redwood): keys are never stored in plaintext, we use envelope encryption. customer master keys stay in your KMS/HSM; only short-lived data-encrypting keys are provisioned to the runtime and rotated. access to KMS is via least-privilege IAM roles and audit logs for all key usage are shipped to the customer's log sink if desired.
[02:20] Samir (Redwood): cc — we'll also share the SOC 2 Type II report and our ISO 27001 cert where available. for the SIG we'll attach the pen test summary and our architecture diagram.
[02:34] Priya (Horizon): procurement will need a copy of the SOC 2 and the DPA redlines; also, data residency — we need confirmation that PII for EU customers stays in eu-west-1 and does not leave region.
[02:50] Jia (Redwood): for hosted API customers we have region routing and can pin region which keeps data in that region. for Dedicated/Private installs you can have full on-prem or VPC control; the control plane metadata still goes to our control plane unless you opt for private control plane which we offer for enterprise. i'll note that in the spreadsheet.
[03:15] Tom (Horizon): how granular is RBAC? can we map to our AD groups?
[03:20] Jia (Redwood): we support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning for groups; RBAC is role-based plus resource scoping — you can sync AD groups via SCIM and map to roles (admin, dev, viewer) and also have per-route policies. we'll demo mapping in the follow-up deep dive.
[03:50] Marta (Horizon): audit logs — retention and content. we need immutable logs for 1 year and a way to export to our SIEM.
[03:58] Jia (Redwood): audit logs are captured at token, request, and infrastructure level. retention is configurable; for hosted customers we keep default 90 days in the console, but we can export to your S3 or GCS or to a SIEM via syslog or push; for enterprise we support longer retention and write-once storage patterns. immutability can be achieved via write-once buckets and object lock.
[04:25] Evan (Horizon): do you provide encryption at rest certificates or evidence for keys in transit? we need TLS cert proof and cipher suites.
[04:32] Jia (Redwood): yes TLS 1.2+ (we prefer 1.3) and we can provide cipher suite documentation, cert chain info, and our pen test covers MITM vectors; we can attach a network encryption spec doc.
[04:50] Samir (Redwood): competitor question — Marta asked if we've done comparisons vs openai / anthropic — we explained our focus is production-grade inference and offering dedicated/private options and fine-grained controls.
[05:10] Marta (Horizon): ok on the SIG section "data flows" we need a diagram showing where logs, cache, and KV cache live and whether any customer data is persisted outside region.
[05:25] Jia (Redwood): right, our runtime uses KV cache for model context; we can configure cache eviction and residency; for hosted we can pin cache regionally; for dedicated it's in your VPC. we'll add a diagram and call out the default TTL and eviction policy.
[06:00] Tom (Horizon): what about PII redaction and transformers? do you provide automated redaction or must we do at the app layer?
[06:10] Jia (Redwood): we have optional prompt-layer redaction helpers and streaming filters; for high assurance we recommend app-side redaction before sending. we do have a data-loss prevention integration pattern as well with hooks to call out-of-band redaction services.
[06:40] Marta (Horizon): regulatory question — would you sign EU data processing addendum with specific subprocessor lists?
[06:50] Samir (Redwood): yes we have a standard DPA and we can provide subprocessor list and SOC 2 evidence; for extra controls we offer private control plane / on-prem deployments. legal (Evan) we can set up a call to go through contract items.
[07:15] Priya (Horizon): timeline: procurement is aiming to close by end of Q3, we might need an initial pilot — what does that look like?
[07:25] Samir (Redwood): pilot typically is a 30–90 day POC on dedicated or hosted depending on requirements; we can allocate dedicated capacity for baseline throughput and collect benchmarks; for security evidence we will produce a tailored package for the pilot.
[07:50] Marta (Horizon): on the SIG there's a question about background checks and personnel security for operators with access to infra, what's your control there?
[07:58] Jia (Redwood): we have background checks for on-call and SREs depending on role, least-privilege access, RBAC, and credential rotation. we can provide our HR security policy excerpt and SOC 2 controls that cover personnel.
[08:20] Tom (Horizon): regarding network segmentation and VPC peering, do you support private endpoints?
[08:26] Jia (Redwood): yes we support private networking options — VPC peering, private endpoints, and for private deployments we can do air-gapped setups. will include network diagram.
[08:45] Marta (Horizon): a few SIG specific notes: we need evidence artifacts mapped to SIG control IDs, like control A.7.1 for personnel, etc. can you pre-map?
[08:55] Samir (Redwood): yes we'll pre-map SOC2/ISO artifacts to SIG controls and send a completed sheet.
[09:10] Evan (Horizon): one legal ask — any subprocessing in third countries? we need list and contractual assurances on data transfers.
[09:20] Jia (Redwood): we maintain a subprocessors registry; any third-country transfers are documented and we can support EU SCCs if needed.
[09:35] Priya (Horizon): for audit logs, can we get sample log entries so our SIEM team can map fields?
[09:40] Jia (Redwood): yes, we have sample log schema and sample events (auth, token creation, model call, cache hit/miss, key use). i'll attach schema and examples.
[10:05] Tom (Horizon): any rate-limiting or throttling that might affect audit fidelity? we need continuous logging even under load.
[10:12] Jia (Redwood): logging is decoupled and buffered — we guarantee eventual delivery to customer sinks and for high-volume customers we can provision dedicated logging pipelines.
[10:35] Marta (Horizon): ok thanks, that mostly covers the high-risk items. one more: how do you handle incident response and breach notification?
[10:45] Samir (Redwood): we have an IR playbook, 72-hour notification for incidents affecting customer data, and we offer an IR tabletop for enterprise customers. we'll include summary IR procedures and contact points.
[11:05] Luis (Redwood CSM): i'll be primary contact during pilot and will coordinate evidence pack uploads.
[11:20] Samir (Redwood): recap and next steps — we'll send the SIG spreadsheet with mapped evidences, SOC2 report, pen test summary, KMS architecture doc, sample logs, and schedule a SSO/SCIM deep dive. legal will coordinate DPA items.
[11:40] Marta (Horizon): sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:50] Samir (Redwood): thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcription: a few speaker labels merged and a couple of product names spelled differently (Redwood Dedicated / Redwood Private spelled in notes). Some pauses and overlaps result in short transcription artifacts.
